name: Karnival

global_influences.evidence: Karnival is explicitly cited as influenced by the Beatles, Pink Floyd and Radiohead among core references shaping its experimental, atmospheric rock direction.
global_influences.source: Last.fm Karnival biography; The Daily Star feature

global_influences.artist_or_genre: Motorhead / Alice in Chains / Nirvana / Oasis
global_influences.evidence: Founders Tinu and Tonmoy set out to create a 'grungy sound,' with Nirvana and Alice in Chains cited as direct grunge-era influences alongside Motorhead and Oasis.
Cited as influences bridging the band's progressive and heavier metal-adjacent experimental tendencies.

local_adaptation_notes: Karnival's stated goal from formation was to create a 'grungy' sound distinct from Bangladesh's dominant metal and mainstream-rock lineages, resulting in Bangla-language material described as highly experimental and 'ahead of their time,' contributing to the country's progressive/experimental rock subgenre alongside acts like Artcell.
sound_evolution_summary: Formative period (2006–2009): started as a passion project among friends aiming for a grunge-inflected sound; achieved a stable lineup by the band's second year and released debut album Indraloy (2009). Consolidation period (2011–2012): key members Khalid Ashraf, Mousum Dhamai and Salmi Rahman joined in 2011, becoming the band's most recognized faces; second album Attotshorgo followed in 2012. Later period: additional releases (Dysfunctional Motion Picture, Mohomukti) continued the band's experimental progressive-rock trajectory.
concert_culture_notes: Associated with Dhaka's progressive/experimental rock circuit; specific concert/festival data not yet documented in available sources — flagged for further research.
listener_community_notes: Recognized within the Bangladeshi rock ecosystem for pushing progressive and experimental metal forward; frequently referenced alongside Shironamhin in related-artist contexts, indicating overlap with the broader alternative/progressive listener base.
